study: Expert pilot v2 - are convention disagreements principled, unstable, or both?
supersedes: v1 (2026-10-15 morning). Replaced BEFORE any annotation existed, after the corpus-proxy test (consistency_summary.py) showed convention disagreements inside ordinary compounds are LESS inconsistent within DCS than agreed cuts, while nominal prefix/negation junctions are MORE inconsistent. v2 tests both patterns on fresh items with experts.
unit: one junction in one written word (one junction per word); 190 items + 10 repeats = 200 rows

groups.D_prefix: 25 disagreement junctions after a nominal prefix/negation (a-, an-, su-, dur-, ku-, sa-, ati-)
groups.C: 40 agreed no-cuts that the Heritage segmenter proposes (control for 'no' answers)

sources: Frontiers evaluation words, held-out DCS words, frequent DCS words (dcs_frequent_eval.csv)
filters: words <= 40 chars, not avagraha-initial; both pieces attested >= 3x as DCS word forms; <= 2 junctions per identical piece (left piece <= 6 in the prefix group)
junction_type: left piece in the nominal-prefix list -> prefix; else DCS compound-member share of the left piece: >= 0.8 compound, <= 0.2 between words
annotators: 2, independent, same items in different orders; they see word (IAST + Devanagari), the marked point and the two pieces; not group, source, model outputs or gold, and are not told the hypotheses

item_measures.either: at least one annotator answered E
item_measures.conflict: one annotator answered Y and the other N or X (hard disagreement)
item_measures.contested: collapsed labels differ (split = Y; no_split = N, X; open = E, U) OR at least one E

predictions.P1_principled: Inside compounds, convention disagreements are principled alternatives: 'either' rate D_compound - A_compound >= 10 points, 95% Newcombe interval lower bound > 0.
predictions.P2_unstable: Prefix/negation disagreements are unstable: 'conflict' rate D_prefix - D_compound >= 10 points, interval lower bound > 0.
predictions.P3_original: Retained from v1 for honesty; the proxy predicts it FAILS. 'contested' rate D - A within compound and between-word junctions, pooled as the mean of the two differences, >= 15 points with bootstrap interval lower bound > 0.

reading: Each prediction: supported (threshold met, interval excludes 0) / not supported (point estimate <= 0) / inconclusive (otherwise). With 25-40 items per cell this is a pilot: only large effects (~20+ points) can reach 'supported'; inconclusive results go to a 400-item run, not into the paper.
secondary: Cohen's kappa on collapsed labels per group
X share per group: X > 30% in a D cell means that cell is dominated by model errors
C vs A 'no' answers as a sanity check that controls behave as expected
quality_check: 10 repeats: per-annotator self-agreement on collapsed labels; < 80% is reported (data kept)
